result.summary: Retains completed and echoed private broadcast transactions in memory and exposes them in the getprivatebroadcastinfo RPC output instead of dropping them upon network echo. Adds a received_by_us object to the RPC response containing the peer address and timestamp when a transaction is received back from the network. When the private broadcast storage hits capacity, the oldest finished transaction is evicted to accommodate new entries.
result.problem: Previously, privately broadcast transactions were pruned from memory once resolved or echoed back from the network. Operators using private broadcast lost visibility into send history, peer acknowledgment times, and echo reception details as soon as the transaction broadcast finished.
evidence: PR description: 'For finished transactions, this allows the inspection of when and to whom the transaction was sent as well as when/if it was echoed from the network.'

Release note: 'The information will now not vanish as soon as the transaction is echoed from the network. In addition getprivatebroadcastinfo returns a received_by_us object for echoed transactions, containing the peer address and time of the reception.'
result.card: Extends getprivatebroadcastinfo to retain and report finished private broadcast transactions rather than dropping them immediately upon network receipt. Adds a received_by_us field indicating the peer address and timestamp when a transaction is echoed back from the network, and evicts the oldest finished transactions when the queue is full. Solves the lack of post-broadcast observability for operators using private transaction broadcast. No dependencies.

risk.why: A bug in queue retention or eviction logic could leak memory or misreport private broadcast confirmation status over RPC.
